messages.subject: Function for tooltip content works for 1 out of 47 observations
messages.subject_clean: Function for tooltip content works for 1 out of 47 observations
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a dataset of corporate twitter accounts and have plotted them using ggvis. I've attached the relevant portion of my dataset if you'd like to reproduce it.
I want to add a tooltip that displays the name of the company attached to each record.
The function below takes the number of followers and correctly returns the company name:

d<-read.csv(data.csv)

f<-function(y){
           m<-as.matrix(d$company,47,1)
           company<-m[which(d$followers==y)]
           company
        }

You can test this by entering f(106000) or f(14700), or any other values from d$followers.

However when I put this function in the add_tooltip function:

p<- d %>% ggvis(~rx,~followers) %>% layer_points()
p %>% add_tooltip(f,"hover")

the plot displays blank tooltips for all datapoints with the exception of the second row in my dataset, Pfizer. Please let me know if you have any ideas as to what I'm doing wrong. Thanks for your interest/help!

Andrew

messages.subject: no able to set layer_rect(width) using band() function
messages.subject_clean: no able to set layer_rect(width) using band() function
messages.body_plain:
Hello again,

I am looking at the examples within the help for the band() function.

Here are the examples:

df <- data.frame(label = c("a", "b", "c"), n = c(10, 9, 4))

base <- df %>% ggvis(~label, y2 = 0, y = ~n)
base %>% layer_rects(width = band())
base %>% layer_rects(width = band(offset = -1))    # no difference
base %>% layer_rects(width = band(mult = 0.9))     # no difference

# A nominal scale with padding is more symmetrical than band with a mult
base %>% layer_rects(width = band(mult = 0.75))    # no difference
base %>% layer_rects(width = band()) %>%           # difference
  scale_nominal("x", padding = 0.25, points = FALSE)

I am not getting any difference among the plots for those cases where band() is used.

I have a use case where I want rectangles with different widths, so setting the scale is not available to me.

I am running the latest github-master version as of this morning.

Thanks as always,

Ian

Thanks,

Ying

Ying

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to plot boxplot with ggvis?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to plot boxplot with ggvis?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ying,

I'm sure Winston and Hadley will have the official "roadmap" answer.

Instead, I can show you what I have done to get something close to a boxplot.

First, I make a function to get the boxplot statistics, taking inspiration from how ggplot2 does it.

library(assertthat)

#' cpt_boxplot
#'
#' This is a first attempt to make boxplots in ggvis
#'
#' @param x     numeric vector to be summarized
#' @param ...   other args passed to boxplot.stats
#'
#' @return data.frame with columns describing boxplot stats
#' @export
#' @import assertthat
#'
cpt_boxplot <- function(x, ...){
  assert_that(is.numeric(x))

  stats <- boxplot.stats(x, ...)$stats

  data.frame(
    whisker_low_ = stats[[1]],
    hinge_low_ = stats[[2]],
    median_ = stats[[3]],
    hinge_high_ = stats[[4]],
    whisker_high_ = stats[[5]]
  )
}

Then I create a plot using those statistics.

```{r}
mt_box <-
  mtcars %>%
  group_by(fcyl = factor(cyl)) %>%
  do(cpt_boxplot(.$mpg))
```

```{r}
mt_box %>%
  ggvis(x = ~fcyl, width = band(), fill := "grey", stroke := "white", strokeWidth := 2) %>%
  layer_rects(y = ~hinge_high_, y2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
  layer_rects(y = ~hinge_low_, y2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
  layer_rects(y = ~hinge_high_, y2 = ~whisker_high_, fillOpacity := 0.25) %>%
  layer_rects(y = ~hinge_low_, y2 = ~whisker_low_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
```

Luckily, switching the axes is no more difficult than the original :)

```{r}
mt_box %>%
  ggvis(y = ~fcyl, height = band(), fill := "grey", stroke := "white", strokeWidth := 2) %>%
  layer_rects(x = ~hinge_high_, x2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
  layer_rects(x = ~hinge_low_, x2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
  layer_rects(x = ~hinge_high_, x2 = ~whisker_high_, fillOpacity := 0.25) %>%
  layer_rects(x = ~hinge_low_, x2 = ~whisker_low_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
```

It should be obvious that this is a complete hack, and that what will be put into ggvis will be **far** superior to this. I really needed a something like a boxplot in ggvis, so this was it.

A couple of notes:

I had to plot the whiskers using boxes because I can't get whiskers made from lines to align with the hinge-boxes.

If you want to plot the outliers, they can be returned from the boxplot.stats function and layers can be made for them.

Hope this helps,

Ian

> >>>   stats <- boxplot.stats(x, ...)$stats
> >>>
> >>>   data.frame(
> >>>     whisker_low_ = stats[[1]],
> >>>     hinge_low_ = stats[[2]],
> >>>     median_ = stats[[3]],
> >>>     hinge_high_ = stats[[4]],
> >>>     whisker_high_ = stats[[5]]
> >>>   )
> >>> }
> >>>
> >>> Then I create a plot using those statistics.
> >>>
> >>> ```{r}
> >>> mt_box <-
> >>>   mtcars %>%
> >>>   group_by(fcyl = factor(cyl)) %>%
> >>>   do(cpt_boxplot(.$mpg))
> >>> ```
> >>>
> >>> ```{r}
> >>> mt_box %>%
> >>>   ggvis(x = ~fcyl, width = band(), fill := "grey", stroke := "white",
> >>> strokeWidth := 2) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(y = ~hinge_high_, y2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(y = ~hinge_low_, y2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(y = ~hinge_high_, y2 = ~whisker_high_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
> >>> %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(y = ~hinge_low_, y2 = ~whisker_low_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
> >>> ```
> >>>
> >>> Luckily, switching the axes is no more difficult than the original :)
> >>>
> >>> ```{r}
> >>> mt_box %>%
> >>>   ggvis(y = ~fcyl, height = band(), fill := "grey", stroke := "white",
> >>> strokeWidth := 2) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(x = ~hinge_high_, x2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(x = ~hinge_low_, x2 = ~median_, fillOpacity := 0.75) %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(x = ~hinge_high_, x2 = ~whisker_high_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
> >>> %>%
> >>>   layer_rects(x = ~hinge_low_, x2 = ~whisker_low_, fillOpacity := 0.25)
> >>> ```
> >>>
> >>> It should be obvious that this is a complete hack, and that what will be
> >>> put into ggvis will be **far** superior to this. I really needed a something
> >>> like a boxplot in ggvis, so this was it.
> >>>
> >>> A couple of notes:
> >>>
> >>> I had to plot the whiskers using boxes because I can't get whiskers made
> >>> from lines to align with the hinge-boxes.
> >>>
> >>> If you want to plot the outliers, they can be returned from the

messages.subject: How to parse a character to add_tooltip() as variable?
messages.subject_clean: How to parse a character to add_tooltip() as variable?
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,

I tried to let users to pick x and y variables for ggvis() from shiny's input_text box. The return from shiny's input_text is a character variable. For example, let's use mtcars, the input_text:

    > input_text
     [1] "mpg"  "cyl"  "disp" "hp"   "drat" "wt"   "qsec" "vs"   "am"
    [10] "gear" "carb"

To plot ggvis(~wt, ~mpg), I can do

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points()

But I have no success to parse input_text to add_tooltip(). I tried

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points() %>% add_tooltip(function(df) df[[input_text[6]]])

    or

    > mtcars %>% ggvis(~mtcars[[input_text[6]]], ~mtcars[[input_text[1]]]) %>% layer_points() %>% add_tooltip(function(df) df$wt)

In both cases, the plot was generated successfully, but add_tooltip() did not work.

Any suggestion?

Thanks a lot,

Ying

messages.subject: ggvis axes in shiny
messages.body_plain:
I'm just starting to use ggvis in shiny and I can't get the axes to work correctly. We have percentage data and we want to show the whole possible range of 0-100 instead of the narrower range of observed values. Instead of putting the axis limits within the plot, it makes a huge range of values and throws the plot on in the spot where the values occur (often found after much scrolling). Here is the relevant code:

library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
...
  mainPanel(
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel("Plot", uiOutput("plot_ui"),
               ggvisOutput("plot"), value="plot"),
    )
  )
))

require(ggvis)
require(dplyr)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  data <- reactive({
    ...
    df
  })

  gv <- reactive({
    data <- data()
      if(is.null(input$county)){
        df <- subset(data, County=="MA")

        df %>% ggvis(~Year, ~Crude.Rate) %>%
          add_axis("y", title="Crude Rate",
                   ticks=11,
                   values=seq(0,100, 10),
                   properties = axis_props(
                     labels = list(
                       fontSize=12),
                     title = list(fontSize=14))) %>%
          add_axis("x", title="Year", format="####") %>%
          layer_points() %>%
          layer_lines() %>%
          add_tooltip(function(df) paste(df$Crude.Rate, ", ", df$Year))
  })
   gv %>% bind_shiny("plot", "plot_ui")
})

Thanks,
Steve

messages.subject: Re: shiny / ggvis data issue
messages.body_plain:
Hi Cory,

I think the problem is that linked_brush() doesn't quite support this
case yet - I didn't think that the original keys and the keys in the
plot might be different. I suspect the code should look something like
this:

df <- mtcars
df$id <- 1:nrow(df)

plot_data <- reactive({
  df$x <- df[,input$x_var]
  # do some dynamic change of the data...

  df <- df[-c(1:runif(1, 1, 10)),]

  df
})

selected_plot_data <- reactive({
  df <- plot_data()
  df$selected <- lb$selected(df$id)
  df
})

lb <- linked_brush(keys = df$id, "red")

Hadley
